reports.title: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM)
reports.description: Malaysia's central statistical authority, responsible for collecting, compiling and disseminating official statistics including national accounts, CPI, labour force and population data; operates the OpenDOSM open-data portal.

reports.title: Malaysia National Accounts / Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
reports.description: Quarterly and annual GDP estimates by production, expenditure and income approaches at current and constant prices, including state-level annual GDP.

reports.title: Malaysia Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring price changes for a fixed basket of goods and services across 13 COICOP-based divisions, disseminated via OpenDOSM.

reports.title: National Institute of Statistics (NIS)
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics, Ministry of Planning, Kingdom of Cambodia
reports.description: Cambodia's national statistics office, responsible for national accounts, CPI, censuses and socio-economic surveys under the Ministry of Planning.

reports.title: Cambodia National Accounts / GDP
reports.description: Annual GDP estimates by production and expenditure approach at current and constant prices, published by NIS.

reports.title: Cambodia Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index using a 12-group classification, published by NIS since 1995.

reports.title: Lao Statistics Bureau (LSB)
reports.publisher: Lao Statistics Bureau, Ministry of Planning and Investment, Lao PDR
reports.description: Lao PDR's national statistics office and focal point for coordination of the national statistical system; disseminates data via the LAOSIS database and a National Summary Data Page under e-GDDS.

reports.title: Lao PDR National Accounts / GDP
reports.description: Annual GDP estimates by production and expenditure approach; the production series is transitioning to 2008 SNA concepts under ISIC Rev. 4 classification.

reports.title: Lao PDR Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index tracking inflation for Lao PDR, published by LSB.

reports.title: Department of Economic Planning and Statistics (DEPS) / Department of Statistics
reports.publisher: Department of Economic Planning and Statistics, Ministry of Finance and Economy, Brunei Darussalam
reports.description: Brunei's official body for national socio-economic statistics; its Department of Statistics compiles and disseminates national accounts, CPI, balance of payments and other official statistics.

reports.title: Brunei Darussalam National Accounts / GDP
reports.description: Quarterly and annual national accounts statistics for Brunei Darussalam covering production, income and expenditure approaches, compiled in accordance with the 1993/2008 System of National Accounts.

reports.title: Brunei Darussalam Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index for Brunei Darussalam, with basket weights revised every five years from the Household Expenditure Survey.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estatistica de Timor-Leste (INETL)
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatistica de Timor-Leste (INETL, I.P.)
reports.description: Timor-Leste's national statistics institute (formerly the General Directorate of Statistics), established as an independent public institute by Decree-Law No. 04/2023; responsible for national accounts, CPI, population and labour statistics.

reports.title: Timor-Leste National Accounts / GDP
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatistica de Timor-Leste (INETL)
reports.description: Annual GDP estimates by expenditure, production and income approach from 2000 onward, in current and constant prices, compiled under 2008 SNA and BPM6.

reports.title: Timor-Leste Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatistica de Timor-Leste (INETL)
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index for Timor-Leste; the current series (Series 3) was introduced in August 2018 using weights from the 2014 Living Standards Survey.

dependencies.basis: Malaysia's IMF DSBB metadata for the National Accounts category states the analytical framework directly, naming the 2008 edition: “The data are compiled in accordance with the methodology set out in the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA).”

Malaysia is a full SDDS subscriber, not merely e-GDDS/SDDS Plus; its 2018 SDDS Annual Report confirms subscription and full compliance: “Malaysia subscribed to the SDDS on August 21, 1996 and met all SDDS requirements on September 1, 2000.”

DOSM's own page on its 2025 ASEAN chairmanship documents Malaysia's leadership role within the ASEAN Community Statistical System: “The establishment of the ASEAN Community during Malaysia's Chairmanship in 2015 marked a historic milestone in the regional integration process.”

The IMF's own numbered press release announces Cambodia's implementation of the enhanced GDDS: “Cambodia Implements the International Monetary Fund's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System” (Press Release No. 18/204, May 30, 2018).

ASEAN's own official ASEAN Key Figures 2025 publication lists Cambodia among its eleven member states: “Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Viet Nam.”

LSB's own National Summary Data Page states Lao PDR's participation in e-GDDS and links its disseminated categories to the IMF DSBB: “Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund's DSBB... the enhanced General Data Dissemination System.”

Lao PDR's DSBB national-accounts metadata (mirrored by ASEANstats, page titled 'GDDS DQAF Base (DSBB) — Lao People's Democratic Republic') explicitly names the 2008 SNA as applicable to the GDP-by-production series: “Lao PDR is currently transitioning to the 2008 SNA and in the tables below, the 2008 SNA is applicable to the series of GDP by Production following the ISIC Rev. 4 classification.”

ASEAN's own official ASEAN Key Figures 2025 publication lists Lao PDR among its eleven member states: “Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Viet Nam.”

Brunei's DSBB national-accounts metadata names a hybrid '1993/2008 System of National Accounts' basis explicitly, so both named editions are wired: “The Department of Statistics (DOS) of the Department of Economic Planning and Statistics (DEPS), Ministry of Finance and Economy is responsible for the compilation and dissemination of the national accounts statistics for Brunei Darussalam in accordance with 1993/2008 System of National Accounts.”
Same DSBB metadata explicitly names 2008 alongside 1993 as the hybrid basis for Brunei's national accounts: “...in accordance with 1993/2008 System of National Accounts.”

DEPS's own National Summary Data Page states its participation in the enhanced GDDS and links disseminated categories to the IMF DSBB: “the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Country participates... Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund's DSBB.”

Brunei's DSBB balance-of-payments metadata states BPM6 is incorporated and closely followed: “The compilation incorporates elements of the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition (BPM6).” ... “The classification system follows closely the recommendations of the BPM6.”

ASEAN's own official ASEAN Key Figures 2025 publication lists Brunei Darussalam among its eleven member states: “Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Viet Nam.”

The IMF's own numbered press release announces Timor-Leste's implementation of the enhanced GDDS: “Timor-Leste Implements the International Monetary Fund's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System” (Press Release No. 19/51, February 19, 2019).

Timor-Leste's own government confirms it formally acceded as ASEAN's eleventh member state on 26 October 2025, updating the prompt's premise that TL was still only an applicant: “October 26, 2025, marks a momentous milestone... As Timor-Leste officially becomes the eleventh member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations at the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur.”

INETL's own current national-accounts page names the 2008 SNA directly as the standard followed: “These are the United Nations System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008) and the International Monetary Fund Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th Edition (BPM6).”

Same INETL national-accounts page names BPM6 directly alongside 2008 SNA as the standards followed: “These are the United Nations System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008) and the International Monetary Fund Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th Edition (BPM6).”

_dropped.why: [COICOP-EDITION] Malaysia's DSBB national-accounts metadata says only 'COICOP is used for household consumption' with no year/edition named. Malaysia's own CPI methodology page (DSBB CPI00) actually lists 13 COICOP divisions including standalone 'Information and Communication' and 'Insurance and Financial Services' groups -- structurally consistent with COICOP 2018, not the 1999 HBS edition Grok picked -- but since no document names an edition explicitly for this country's release, per the edition-matching rule neither un-coicop-2018 nor un-coicop-hbs-1999 is minted.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] Grok's only source for this claim was a Phnom Penh Post news article quoting an NIS official -- a news-summary site, disallowed as a citation under project rules. I could not find an NIS or IMF primary document independently confirming a current SNA edition: NIS's own national-accounts page (nis.gov.kh/en/national/) shows GDP tables from 2014 onward but states no methodology edition, and the only primary metadata I could find (IMF DSBB NAG00 for KHM, and UNSD's Cambodia national-accounts info page) both describe SNA 1993 with a 2000 base year and 'in progress' 2008 SNA implementation, apparently stale but not affirmatively overridden by any primary source I could locate. Genuinely ambiguous -- dropping rather than guessing.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] Proposed node was sourced only from a Phnom Penh Post article (disallowed news aggregator). No NIS or government primary page describing this specific 2014 base-year rebase could be found (NIS's technical-documents page lists only CSIC-v2 and CSCO-v1, nothing on national-accounts rebasing). Dropping the node rather than minting on an unverifiable claim.

[COICOP-EDITION] Both the 2012 TL-NA methodological volume and the current DSBB TLS/NAG00 metadata state household consumption is 'classified according to the COICOP at level 3 classes' with no year/edition named. Not enough to pick 1999 HBS vs. 2018 per the edition-matching rule, despite the document's 2012 vintage suggesting the older edition -- that reasoning alone isn't sufficient grounds to mint.

[CONTAINMENT] Verified this is a genuine primary document (Timor-Leste Ministry of Finance, National Directorate of Statistics, April 2012, 'TL-NA 2004-2010 Volume II: Methodological Notes'), but it is a methodological companion volume to the TL-NA 2004-2010 release, not a distinct recurring or one-off publication in its own right -- it documents the same report already proposed as tl-national-accounts. Used its content (cross-checked against INETL's current national-accounts page) to support the tl-national-accounts -> sna-2008 / imf-bpm6 edges instead of minting a separate node.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] Grok's batch2 evidence_url (a DEPS-hosted Supply-Use-Table-Summary.pdf) does contain the SNA-2008 sentence quoted, but on inspection it is generic international boilerplate describing what Supply-and-Use Tables are worldwide ('jointly produced by the United Nations, IMF, World Bank, OECD and the EU'), not a Brunei-specific adoption statement. I still mint bn-national-accounts -> sna-2008 (and -> sna-1993) but on the stronger, country-specific DSBB NAG00 metadata quote instead ('...in accordance with 1993/2008 System of National Accounts').
